title: Ansel and the Parish
premise: When retired detective Paloma Amberdale receives a confession letter postmarked the day after Edmund Vasse's funeral, he recognizes the handwriting as his own—a letter he never wrote. The letter claims responsibility for a drowning thirty years ago at the Vasse estate, the case that ended Paloma's career and drove him to hide among secondhand books. As the Vasse family gathers for the thirtieth anniversary dinner, Paloma discovers the letter was forged by someone who knows exactly how he investigates, forcing him to reconstruct old alibis while dodging a killer who is rewriting the past in his name. The trail leads to the family's youngest heir, who witnessed the drowning as a child and has spent decades curating everyone's memories—including Paloma's—until the anniversary toast becomes the stage for a confession no forged letter could contain.
about_author: Cyrus Thackeray spent a decade as a parish records clerk in coastal Norfolk before turning to crime fiction, a career he describes as 'reading other people's endings for a living.' He writes in a converted vestry and claims he can date any lie by its ink.

chapters.title: Postmark
chapters.summary: Paloma Amberdale, sorting a dead author's estate into his failing bookshop, receives a confession letter in his own handwriting, postmarked the day after Edmund Vasse's funeral. His POV. The emotional beat is cold recognition—the past knocking with his own knuckles.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Paloma rereads the letter and finds details only the original investigator could know. Flashback to his disgrace fifteen years ago. His POV. Emotional beat: shame resurfacing like water damage on a beloved spine.

chapters.title: Mourning in Good Order
chapters.summary: Paloma attends the Vasse memorial, observing the heirs: eldest son Alistair, brittle daughter-in-law Maren, and the reclusive youngest, Isolde. Third-person limited on Paloma. Emotional beat: watching a family perform grief like a rehearsed play.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Paloma revisits the cove where Thomas Vasse drowned thirty years ago and finds a fresh footprint too small to be his own. His POV. Emotional beat: the dread of realizing someone is retracing his steps.

chapters.title: Alistair's Ledger
chapters.summary: Alistair hires Paloma privately to find who sent the letter, insisting his father died innocent. Paloma accepts to get inside the house. Alistair's POV. Emotional beat: a son's desperate need to buy back a clean inheritance.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Paloma rebuilds the original case files from memory: four guests, four alibis, all woven tight. He finds the seam—Maren's mother's testimony, since recanted. His POV. Emotional beat: the old detective reflex waking, painful and sweet.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Caller
chapters.summary: A stranger buys every book Paloma owns on the Vasse case, paying in old banknotes from thirty years ago. Paloma's assistant Wren saw his face. Wren's POV. Emotional beat: a young employee realizing her quiet employer is a mystery himself.

chapters.title: Isolde's Greenhouse
chapters.summary: Isolde, tending her late father's orchids, speaks to Paloma in careful, curated sentences—too careful. Her POV. Emotional beat: the loneliness of someone who has rehearsed every conversation for decades.

chapters.title: Ink and Water
chapters.summary: A document examiner confirms the confession was written with aged paper and period ink—by someone patient. Paloma suspects a forger trained in archival work. His POV. Emotional beat: admiration and fear braided together.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Maren receives a letter threatening to expose her mother's recanted testimony before the anniversary dinner. She begs Paloma to bury it. Maren's POV. Emotional beat: the corrosion of a marriage built on a protected lie.

chapters.title: Wren's Discovery
chapters.summary: Wren finds a photograph hidden in returned stock: young Paloma at the cove the week of the drowning, with a child beside him. Wren confronts him. Wren's POV. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking against curiosity.

chapters.title: The Child at the Cove
chapters.summary: Paloma admits he was there that summer—tutoring the Vasse children—and that the child in the photo was Isolde. His POV, half confession. Emotional beat: the weight of a memory he chose not to keep.

chapters.title: Alistair's Mistake
chapters.summary: Alistair, panicking, burns papers in the estate fireplace; Paloma salvages a half-scorched page of Isolde's handwriting that mimics his own. Alistair's POV. Emotional beat: a man destroying his own alibi to save his name.

chapters.title: Curator of Memory
chapters.summary: Paloma realizes Isolde has spent thirty years collecting letters, photographs, and testimony—archiving the family like rare editions. His POV. Emotional beat: the chill of meeting a mind that files people.

chapters.title: The Recantation
chapters.summary: Paloma tracks down Maren's mother, now in a care home, who admits she was paid to change her story—by Edmund himself. Her POV. Emotional beat: an old woman's guilt finally spending itself.

chapters.title: What Edmund Knew
chapters.summary: Edmund's private diary, obtained through the solicitor, reveals he knew Thomas's death was no accident and protected the killer for thirty years. Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: the vertigo of a victim who was also an accomplice.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: The Vasse heirs gather for the thirtieth-anniversary dinner; the forged letter's author promised a toast. Paloma attends as Alistair's guest. Third-person limited. Emotional beat: a table set like a trap.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Isolde rises to toast her father and instead recounts the drowning in perfect detail, watching each guest's face. Alistair breaks; Maren flees. Isolde's POV. Emotional beat: thirty years of curation detonating in one speech.

chapters.title: Confession, Corrected
chapters.summary: Isolde admits she forged Paloma's letter to force the family into the open—she was the child at the cove, and she saw her brother Alistair hold Thomas under. Isolde's POV. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into truth-telling.

chapters.title: Alistair's Silence
chapters.summary: Confronted, Alistair confesses: a boyish shove during a quarrel, and a father who chose inheritance over justice, buying silence with everyone's future. Alistair's POV. Emotional beat: relief and ruin arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: Filing the Truth
chapters.summary: Paloma hands the evidence to a young constable who once idolized him, refusing to bury it again. Isolde chooses to stay and face the town. Paloma's POV. Emotional beat: a man finally filing the truth instead of hiding it.

chapters.title: The Last Shelf
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Paloma reopens the bookshop with Wren as partner, shelving the Vasse case files openly in the window. A letter arrives from Isolde—thank you, in her own hand. His POV. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; memory finally alphabetized.
